reference: The club. The back room. The interrogation in the kitchen. This is the game's Sopranos wing.
diagnosis: The NPCs in this club are written well — the bartender is not a shelf, the slot machine attacked somebody, Snow likes the cold. The Prospect standing in front of them is written like a dialogue menu. Almost every weak line in this scene is his: 'What have you got?' 'I understand.' 'Noted for the record.' 'Good to see you too, Boosk.' He is the one character with nothing to say in a room where everybody else is specific. Second problem: the interrogation goes polite exactly when it should go cold — you do not ask a man you have just worked over with kitchen equipment why he didn't mention it sooner.

lines.current: Please don't make me a bit.
lines.why: CUT — 'a bit' is meta-comedy slang that acknowledges the game's own joke structure. Doctrine violation, same family as the Counter-Strike line.
lines.house: Whatever this is, I'm not doing it.
lines.tarantino: Whatever's about to happen, I want it in the record that I said no. Out loud. In front of people.
lines.mcdonagh: No. Whatever that is, no. I've seen your face doin' that before and it never ends well for me.
lines.houser: Absolutely not. Whatever this is, I decline, and I'd like that reflected in the minutes.
lines.coen: No. I don't — whatever this is, I'd rather not. Thank you, though.

lines.current: I know what I'm doing.
lines.why: The single most generic tough-guy line available, said to Big Uncle Lou of all people, who would eat it.
lines.house: I've got it. I know how it looks. I've got it.
lines.tarantino: I know what I'm doing. And I know that's exactly what a man who doesn't know what he's doing says. I'm saying it anyway.
lines.mcdonagh: I know what I'm at. I know that's what an eejit says. I'm sayin' it regardless.
lines.houser: I've got a handle on it. And yes, I hear how that sounds, and no, I don't have a better sentence.
lines.coen: I know what I'm doing. I do. I've thought about it some.

lines.current: I understand.
lines.why: A confirm button. Lou has just warned him about something serious and the kid has no reaction to it.
lines.house: I hear you. I don't like it, but I hear you.
lines.tarantino: I understand. I want to be clear that understanding it and liking it are two different rooms, and I'm only standing in one of them.
lines.mcdonagh: I understand you. I don't have to be happy about it, but I understand you.
lines.houser: Understood. And noted. And filed somewhere I'm going to be looking at for a while.
lines.coen: I understand. I don't know that I agree. But I understand it.

lines.current: What’s good back there that isn’t going to kill me?
lines.why: Default RPG bar dialogue. The bartender here has real personality; the kid should be talking to a person, not a vendor menu.
lines.house: What's good back there that isn't going to kill me?
lines.tarantino: What have you got that a man can drink standing up, without a conversation about it.
lines.mcdonagh: What've you got? And don't be showin' me the bottle with the dust on it, I've seen where that's been.
lines.houser: What's on offer that won't ruin my evening or my liver, in that order?
lines.coen: What've you got back there? I'm not fussy. I'd just rather not have the one from last time.
lines.picked: What’s good back there that isn’t going to kill me?

lines.current: One for the road.
lines.why: Stock phrase with no world in it.
lines.house: Last one. I've got a thing.
lines.tarantino: One more. And then I've got a thing, and I'd rather do the thing with one in me than none.
lines.mcdonagh: One more and I'm away. I've a job on, and it's the kind you'd want a drink in you for.
lines.houser: One more for the commute. I've got an appointment that's going to require a certain flexibility of conscience.
lines.coen: One more, then I'll get going. I've got something I've got to do.

lines.current: Anything I should know before I go back there?
lines.why: Exposition-fishing. Video-gamey 'give me the quest info' phrasing.
lines.house: What kind of mood is he in back there?
lines.tarantino: Before I go back there. What's the weather like. And I'm asking a man who has watched a lot of people walk back there.
lines.mcdonagh: What's the form back there? You've watched a lot of fellas go through that door, you'd know.
lines.houser: Give me the room back there. Mood, headcount, and whether anybody's already unhappy before I make it worse.
lines.coen: Anything I ought to know before I head back? You'd know better than me.

lines.current: Good to see you too, Boosk.
lines.why: Courteous nothing against a loud, huge character. This relationship is the emotional spine of the whole game and this is a handshake.
lines.house: You smell like a fire in a butcher's, Boosk.
lines.tarantino: Good to see you too. You're louder than last time. I didn't think there was room for louder.
lines.mcdonagh: Good to see you and all. You've gotten louder. I didn't think that was available to you.
lines.houser: Good to see you, Boosk. You've somehow gotten bigger, which I was told was not physically possible.
lines.coen: Good to see you too, Boosk. You look — yeah. You look about the same.

lines.current: I came straight in.
lines.why: Filler, and it sits right beside 'Your slot machine attacked me,' which shows exactly how good this beat can be.
lines.house: I came straight in. Nobody stopped me, which I'd look into.
lines.tarantino: Came straight in. Nobody stopped me. Walked past four of your guys and a door that's supposed to be locked, and here I am.
lines.mcdonagh: Came straight in. Nobody stopped me. You'd want to look at that, or someone less lovely than me'll do the same.
lines.houser: I walked straight in. Past two doors and four employees. That's a security review right there and I'm giving it to you free.
lines.coen: I came right in. Nobody said anything. I thought that was worth mentioning.

lines.current: I’ll write that on my hand.
lines.why: Corporate-sounding acknowledgment. Ape is the best-written character in the game and deserves a scene partner.
lines.house: I'll write that on my hand.
lines.tarantino: Noted. Filed. Alphabetised. I'll be carrying that one around for a while.
lines.mcdonagh: Noted. That's goin' straight in the vault with the rest of your wisdom.
lines.houser: Noted, logged, and added to the growing document of things you've said to me that I'll need therapy about.
lines.coen: Noted. I'll remember that. I remember most of what you say, actually.
lines.picked: I’ll write that on my hand.

lines.current: Then I won't keep him.
lines.why: Butler politeness from a mob prospect to a doorman.
lines.house: Then I'll be quick and he won't have to look at me long.
lines.tarantino: Then I won't keep him. I'll be in and out so fast he'll think he imagined it.
lines.mcdonagh: Then I'll not keep him. I'll be in and gone before he's finished disapprovin' of me.
lines.houser: Then I'll be brief. Nobody's ever complained that I took up too little of their evening.
lines.coen: Then I won't keep him long. I know he's busy. Everybody's busy.

lines.current: You look like you haven't slept.
lines.why: Bland table-setting. Aubbie is running herself into the ground; the observation should be specific and a little cruel, which is how people in this world show they care.
lines.house: You look like you've been awake since Tuesday and lost the argument.
lines.tarantino: You've got the face. The one people get around hour forty. I've seen it on men doing much worse work than this.
lines.mcdonagh: You look shockin'. I mean that kindly. You look like somethin' that's been left out.
lines.houser: You look like an HR case that hasn't been filed yet. Does this place have a maximum shift or is that just a thing other businesses have?
lines.coen: You look like you haven't slept. I don't mean anything by it. You just — you look like that.

lines.current: Get some sleep, Aubbie.
lines.why: Toothless concern. It should be affection expressed the only way anyone in this family knows how — as an instruction with a threat shape.
lines.house: Go home, Aubbie. I'll tell him you were here till two and he can argue with me about it.
lines.tarantino: Go home. And if anybody asks where you went, they can come find me, and I'll explain it to them at length.
lines.mcdonagh: Go home to bed. And if anyone gives out about it, send them to me and I'll give out back at them.
lines.houser: Go home, Aubbie. Sleep is not a benefit this organization offers, so you'll have to steal it like everything else.
lines.coen: Get some sleep, Aubbie. Go on. Somebody's got to be the one who says it.

lines.current: Let’s start with money. Not names, money. Who paid you? how, and did it clear?
lines.why: Stock interrogation. Every other option in this beat has specificity — the hair, the silver case, the car — and this one has none.
lines.house: Whose money is in your shoes?
lines.tarantino: Let's start with money. Not names — money. Who paid you, how, and did it clear.
lines.mcdonagh: Who's payin' you? And don't say a name, say an amount. The amount tells me the name.
lines.houser: Who's funding you? And I want the entity, not the individual, because the individual's always some idiot with a clipboard.
lines.coen: Who hired you? I'd like to know that. It'd save everybody some time.
lines.picked: Let’s start with money. Not names, money. Who paid you? how, and did it clear?

lines.current: Who sent you into our city?
lines.why: 'Our city' reads like a placeholder from a different, worse game.
lines.house: Who put you on a plane to this shithole?
lines.tarantino: Somebody put you on a plane. Somebody looked at a map, found this place, and thought: him. I want that person's name and I want to know what they were drinking.
lines.mcdonagh: Who sent you here? To here. Have you seen here? Someone hated you enough to send you here.
lines.houser: Who deployed you? Because somebody sat in an office and decided this town was worth an operative, and I'd love to see that business case.
lines.coen: Who sent you out here? Somebody had to send you. Nobody comes here on their own.

lines.current: Who inside the family are you talking to?
lines.why: Generic phrasing for the single most important question in the scene.
lines.house: Which one of ours has been talking to you? Say the name and this stops.
lines.tarantino: Somebody in that room upstairs has been talking to you. I've eaten with those men. I want a name, and then I want to go and sit down.
lines.mcdonagh: Which of ours is talkin' to you? I've had me dinner with every one of them. Say a name and ruin me evenin'.
lines.houser: Who's your inside line? Because I've got a room full of people upstairs and one of them's a subscription service.
lines.coen: Who're you talking to inside? Somebody is. That's just — that's the only way any of this works.

lines.current: That was available the entire time. Every minute of the last hour was elective. I hope you understand that’s a choice you made.
lines.why: Curiously polite, immediately after torturing a confession out of a man. The kid should be cold here, or genuinely rattled — not conversational.
lines.house: You had that in you the whole time. All of that, for that.
lines.tarantino: You had that the whole time. That whole name was sitting in you while we did all of this. I want you to think about how much of the last hour was optional.
lines.mcdonagh: You had that in you the whole time. All that carry-on, and it was in you the whole while. That's on you, that is.
lines.houser: That was available the entire time. Every minute of the last hour was elective. I hope you understand that's a choice you made.
lines.coen: You had that the whole time. Huh. That's — that's a hell of a thing to sit on.
lines.picked: That was available the entire time. Every minute of the last hour was elective. I hope you understand that’s a choice you made.
lines.retiredText: Why didn't you tell us before?

lines.current: Leave the cart alone.
lines.why: Flat command sitting next to genuinely great options — the tongs, the ice bucket, the meat tenderiser. This one should be a choice with a reason in it.
lines.house: Cart stays where it is. He can look at it.
lines.tarantino: Leave the cart. Let him look at it. A man looking at a cart does more work in five minutes than I could do in an hour.
lines.mcdonagh: Leave the cart. Let him have a good look at it. That's half the job done and I've not lifted a thing.
lines.houser: Cart stays. Let him inventory it himself. Anticipation is free and I'm running a business.
lines.coen: Leave the cart alone. Just let him see it. That's usually enough, in my experience.

lines.current: You still with us, Numbskull? Blink if the answer’s no.
lines.why: A soft check-in with no edge and no humour, in a scene built entirely on kitchen-equipment menace.
lines.house: You still with us, Numbskull? Blink if the answer's no.
lines.tarantino: You holding up? And be honest, because there's a lot of night left and I need to know what I'm working with.
lines.mcdonagh: Are you alive in there, Numbskull? Give us a blink if you're not.
lines.houser: How are we doing, Numbskull? And I mean that operationally, not emotionally, because we don't do emotionally down here.
lines.coen: You holding up okay, Numbskull? It's been a long one. For everybody.
lines.picked: You still with us, Numbskull? Blink if the answer’s no.

lines.current: Did you actually go through it, or did you look at it and get bored?
lines.why: Managerial check-in tone in a room where a man is tied to a chair.
lines.house: Did you actually go through it, or did you look at it and get bored?
lines.tarantino: Did you go through it properly. And I want you to understand that 'properly' in this room means seams, shoes, and the lining, not a glance and a shrug.
lines.mcdonagh: Did you go through it right? Or did you have a wee look and lose interest, like you do.
lines.houser: Did you conduct an actual search, or the thing you do where you pat a bag and call it due diligence?
lines.coen: Did you go through it all the way? Because last time you went through it, you didn't go through it.
lines.picked: Did you actually go through it, or did you look at it and get bored?
lines.retiredText: Did you go through it properly?

lines.current: Anything on there worth anything?
lines.why: Interchangeable with any heist scene in any game.
lines.house: Anything on there worth the night we're having?
lines.tarantino: Anything on there worth what this has cost us? And I'm counting the towels.
lines.mcdonagh: Is there anythin' on it worth the state of this room?
lines.houser: Is there anything of value on it, or have we destroyed a functioning kitchen for a man's holiday photos?
lines.coen: Anything on there worth anything? Because this has been a lot of trouble already.

lines.current: What have you already tried?
lines.why: Purely functional information-gathering, in a scene whose whole comic engine is treating an interrogation like a cooking show.
lines.house: What have you tried so far, and why is it all still on the counter?
lines.tarantino: Walk me through what you've already tried. In order. Because from where I'm standing it looks like you've tried everything at once, which isn't a method, it's a mess.
lines.mcdonagh: What've you tried so far? And be honest, because I can see the counter and the counter's tellin' me a story.
lines.houser: What's been attempted so far? Give me the process. I'd like to know whether we're being systematic or just enthusiastic.
lines.coen: What have you tried already? I just don't want to repeat anything. That'd be a waste.

lines.current: Why can't you do this yourself?
lines.why: Flat and functional with no attitude behind it.
lines.house: Why is this mine? You've got two hands and a whole kitchen.
lines.tarantino: Explain to me why this is my job. You have two hands, a full kitchen, and about forty years on me.
lines.mcdonagh: Why's it me? You've the hands. You've the kitchen. You've the years. Why's it always me?
lines.houser: Why is this being delegated to me? You have the tools, the expertise, and, I'd argue, the temperament.
lines.coen: Why can't you do it yourself? I'm asking sincerely. You seem better suited.

lines.current: They’re alive, which this week counts.
lines.why: A non-answer with no payoff.
lines.house: They're alive, which this week counts.
lines.tarantino: They're alright. Which this month is a genuinely impressive answer.
lines.mcdonagh: They're grand. Well. They're breathin'. That's what grand means now.
lines.houser: They're fine. And by fine I mean nobody's in a hole, which is the current standard.
lines.coen: They're all right. Everybody's — yeah. Everybody's all right.
lines.picked: They’re alive, which this week counts.

lines.current: You want them to turn the heat up?
lines.why: Weak small talk that wastes Snow's setup — Snow says it's cold in here and likes it. The comeback should engage the strangeness.
lines.house: You like it cold. That's a whole thing about you, isn't it.
lines.tarantino: You like it cold. I've noticed that. You're the only man I know who books a table by temperature.
lines.mcdonagh: You like it freezin'. That's not normal. I'm not sayin' it's wrong, I'm sayin' it's not normal.
lines.houser: You actually like it cold. That's not a preference, that's a condition, and I'd like it looked at.
lines.coen: You like it cold. Huh. Most people don't. But you do.

lines.current: Lou's in the back. He said don't make him wait.
lines.why: Plain relay with none of this bartender's flavour — the same man says 'I am not a shelf' and 'it makes the hands weird'.
lines.house: Lou's in the back. He said don't make him wait, and he said it in the voice.
lines.tarantino: Lou's in the back. He said don't make him wait. He said it twice, and the second time he said it to nobody, which is how I knew he meant it.
lines.mcdonagh: Lou's out the back. He said don't be keepin' him. And he'd the face on, so.
lines.houser: Lou's in the back. His exact words were don't make him wait, and his exact tone was the one that ends careers.
lines.coen: Lou's in the back. He said not to make him wait. I'd take him at his word on that.

lines.current: Why give me this here?
lines.why: Functional question that undersells the tension of a briefing happening somewhere it should not be happening.
lines.house: Why are we doing this out here, where anybody can see us doing it?
lines.tarantino: Why here? There's forty people out that door and a girl on a pole eight feet from your head. Why is this the room you picked.
lines.mcdonagh: Why here? There's half the county out that door. Why's this the room you chose for it?
lines.houser: Why are we having this conversation here? There's a public on the other side of that curtain and a camera in the corner I don't recognise.
lines.coen: Why're you giving me this here? There's people right out there. That's all I'm saying.

lines.current: What is at room twelve?
lines.why: Flat and incurious, delivered immediately after a brutal beating at the party. The kid does not react at all to what just happened.
lines.house: What's in room twelve? And don't tell me on the way, tell me now, because I've had a night.
lines.tarantino: What's in room twelve. And before you answer — I've just watched a man get taken apart at a party. So take your time and pick your words, because I'm not in a good place for a surprise.
lines.mcdonagh: What's in room twelve? And say it now, not in the car. I've had enough of findin' things out in cars.
lines.houser: What's in room twelve? And I'd like the full brief, not the version where I find out the important part while I'm holding something.
lines.coen: What's at room twelve? I'd like to know before we go. That's not — I don't think that's unreasonable.

lines.current: That’s a bust. The house doesn’t feel anything about it.
lines.why: A mob-club dealer apologising undercuts the house's cold energy, which the sibling line ('The house always liked me better') gets right.
lines.house: That's a bust. The house doesn't feel anything about it.
lines.tarantino: Bust. And I want you to know I felt nothing. Twenty-two years, and I have never once felt anything.
lines.mcdonagh: Bust. I'd say I'm sorry but I'd be lyin' and we've enough of that in here.
lines.houser: Bust. The house thanks you for your contribution to the renovation fund.
lines.coen: That's a bust. Yeah. These things happen.
lines.picked: That’s a bust. The house doesn’t feel anything about it.
